page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2ne.8xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core. A key hardware feature is its bundled local storage, consisting of 7679 GB of SSD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear division between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the bottom 25% tier, and single-threaded operations like gzip compression are weak. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as shown by stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression tests. Memory bandwidth for both read and write operations on large blocks remains in the average tier, though the PassMark memory score is relatively weak.

Given the high density of local SSD storage paired with 256 GB of RAM, this instance offers a specialized hardware profile where storage capacity and memory volume are prioritized over raw single-core compute speed. This makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads that require large local data footprints without needing high-frequency CPU cores. Appropriate workloads include relational and non-relational databases, caching layers like Redis, static web serving, and general-purpose multi-threaded applications.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2ne.8xlarge is an x86_64 server featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8163 processor, 256.0 GB of RAM, and a substantial 7679 GB of bundled local SSD storage. Operating on a KVM hypervisor, it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps. Performance benchmarks show a contrast between weak single-core execution and average multi-core processing capabilities. Memory read and write bandwidths remain in the average tier, while database and Redis SET operations also demonstrate average throughput. Lacking a GPU, this instance is not designed for hardware-accelerated tasks. Instead, its high storage-to-vCPU ratio and large memory footprint make it highly suitable for storage-intensive and database workloads, such as large-scale caching, data indexing, and relational databases that benefit from massive local SSD capacity and moderate multi-threaded compute power.
